title: Claim: Home Ministry Agniveer portal data offered for sale, Mathrubhumi reports; no official confirmation
date_note: Mathrubhumi's publication day; the page says details of the September incident only now emerged and gives no earlier disclosure day.
place: India (country as stated; location of the portal not given)
geo_basis: country level; Delhi Police named as the investigator, no victim site location stated
summary: Mathrubhumi reports that data found with a 14-year-old from Haryana, including personal details of more than 2500 Agniveers and admin credentials, was advertised for sale at $500 in cryptocurrency. Police sources said a letter asked the Home Ministry to examine it, and the page says there has been no official confirmation. It says the hacker was questioned and a case registered under the IT Act.
plain: An Indian newspaper reports a teenager advertised Agniveer recruits' personal details for sale. The Home Ministry has not confirmed it, and it is unclear whether the data is genuine.
exec: Unconfirmed report of defence-recruit personal data offered for sale; the Home Ministry has not confirmed it.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Mathrubhumi says police sources asked the Home Ministry to verify the data.
impact: Reported personal details of more than 2500 Agniveers; authenticity not confirmed.

sources.name: Mathrubhumi: 14-year-old hacks Home Ministry portal; Agniveers' details on dark web

validation.note: Single publisher (Mathrubhumi, Malayalam); relies on unnamed police sources; the page says there is no official confirmation and that authenticity is unclear.
